thread:
maya: Heads up — provisioning queue in us-west-2 just spiked, ~250 pending GPU allocations. Seeing a bunch of nodes in 'maintenance' after OOB power cycles.

devon: on it. any common failure mode in the logs? secureboot toggles maybe?

maya: yes, we have ~40 nodes where BMC reported a firmware apply, then secure-boot state went from 'disabled' -> 'enabled' (unexpected). NTP also shows a ~12s jump around the same time.

ops-bot: alert: oob-vlan-connstorm detected on oob-switch-3; 03:21 UTC — event rate 5k/min. Correlated: 40 bmc-heartbeat-lost, 38 bmc-rebooted

liam: if secureboot flips during boot after a firmware apply some machines fall back to recovery, causing provisioning to retry and pile up. Suggest marking affected racks DRAIN and routing new jobs elsewhere.

arjun: we need quick mitigation: Can we disable OOB management VLAN on the affected leaf to stop the connection storm? That'll break remote KVM for a bit but will stop flapping.

devon: put a temp ACL on the oob switch (deny BMC broadcast). Also running a quick grep on ipmitool output: ``for i in $(cat nodes); do ipmitool -H $i raw 0x30 0x45; done`` shows mixed secure-boot flags.

maya: ACL applied. I've started draining rack-r5 and rerouting allocations. New allocations to us-west-1 and eu-west until we stabilize.

liam: can we roll back the firmware batch? Which version pushed? If it was a microcode + BMC combo that toggles policy, rollback might be fastest.

devon: version is bmcfw-2.14.7+secure-policy-a. We can schedule rollback but it will take ~6h for full rack. For immediate relief, disabling NTP step on the BMCs to stop the leap might prevent further toggles.

arjun: note: disabling NTP will fail compliance checks for a short window — get an exception ticket if it looks like we'll be offline >30m. Also cost note: rerouting to other regions is increasing spot burn — projected extra $2.3k for next 24h if we keep this.

maya: agreed, opened ticket INF-4932 for exception. I'm running a parallel job to patch the NTP config on affected BMCs: ``sed -i 's/pool 0.pool.ntp.org/0.pool.ntp.org iburst/' /etc/ntp.conf && systemctl restart ntpd``

liam: we should also add a gate to the firmware rollout: abort if >1% of nodes report secure-boot state change within 10m. That would've caught this rollout.

devon: capture: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-logs/infra/4067891234/bmc-flip.tar.gz. I'm tagging all affected nodes with tag=oob-flip-4067891234 and creating a k8s node affinity to avoid scheduling there.

ops-bot: update: drain 12/14 nodes in rack-r5 complete; provisioning backlog reduced to 42 pending. Continuing to monitor.

maya: thanks everyone. Postmortem prep please — include rollout gating, NTP hardening, and a temporary cost cap on cross-region failover. I'll update runbook with the ACL step.

arjun: assigning follow-ups: rollback plan (liam), ntp hardening playbook (devon), gating rules (maya). We'll do a blameless review tomorrow.

liam: FYI adding a quick snippet for runbook: ``# emergency oob ACL
ssh oob-switch-3 'configure terminal; interface vlan 10; shutdown; exit; write memory'``

maya: nice. closing ops for now — monitoring channel and paging team if it creeps again. :thumbsup:
